grade_reason: No statement by him about AI risk, and no quotable statement about AI at all, was found in news reports or on his official site.
notes: All 8 web searches ran (the 6 required plus one on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors and one general search). None of the searches found any statement by him on superintelligence, extinction, a pause or slowdown, a China agreement or AI safety. The site-restricted search returned no pages from desjarlais.house.gov. The earlier attempt opened https://desjarlais.house.gov/news/ (10 most recent releases, 28 February 2025 to 1 October 2026, none about AI) and the 10 April 2025 Strategic Forces hearing release (no mention of AI). This run also opened https://desjarlais.house.gov/media-center?page=2 (releases from June 2023 to 20 January 2025), with no titles about AI. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced by Rep. Casar on 24 September 2026): the sources found name only Democratic cosponsors and none name DesJarlais, but no complete official cosponsor list was opened, so this is not confirmed. A search-result summary says a Dailymotion video (https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x9i9bts) shows him questioning military officials about AI for military use at a House Armed Services hearing dated 21 April 2025. The video page could not be read and there is no quotable wording. Military use would be level D under ruling 3 in any case. If a reviewer confirms it, the grade could be changed from none to D. The newschannel9.com article 'AI risks are getting harder for Congress to ignore' was opened and does not mention him. The wtop.com article on a lawmakers' AI meeting returned 404. Hearing transcripts and congress.gov cosponsor pages were not checked directly.
